title: A febrile patient in the emergency department
intro: A 68-year-old woman comes in with fever, rigors and confusion since this morning. Heart rate 112, blood pressure 98/60, respiratory rate 24. It could be a viral illness (60 % of similar patients) or a bacterial sepsis (40 %). You decide what to do and when: draw lactate and blood cultures, start antibiotics, give two litres of fluid, or order a CT scan. Before any result, and again when the lactate comes back, say how likely you think sepsis is. The case runs for six hours; the patient's course follows your decisions.
ctLabel: CT scan of the chest and abdomen (at 15 min)
est0Label: Your probability of sepsis on arrival
est1Label: Your probability of sepsis once the lactate is back
pSLabel: Probability of sepsis given what you learnt
errLabel: How far your estimates were from it
